questions.stem: A sample has a half-life of 6.0 hours; find the decay constant in per hour.
questions.explanation: Using lambda equals ln2 divided by half-life gives 0.693 over 6.0 hours. The tempting idea of dividing 1 by 6 ignores the logarithmic nature of decay.

questions.stem: A source has half-life 10 days; how many days until its activity is one fifth?
questions.explanation: t equals t_half times ln5 over ln2, giving 10 times 1.609 over 0.693. Simply counting two half-lives would only reach one quarter, not one fifth.

questions.explanation: Activity equals lambda N, with N from mass over molar mass times Avogadro. Using lambda as 1 over half-life would understate the true activity by a factor of ln2.

questions.stem: The mean life of a radionuclide is related to its half-life by which expression?

options.text: Mean life equals half-life divided by ln 2.
options.misconception: inverts the correct ratio of mean life to half-life

options.text: Mean life equals half-life times ln 2.
options.misconception: multiplies instead of dividing by ln 2

options.text: It is the probability per unit time that a given nucleus decays
It is the time for half the nuclei to decay
It increases as the sample ages
options.misconception: thinks decay constant changes with remaining amount

options.text: It equals the fraction decayed after one second

questions.topic: Net count rate after three half-lives of the source
questions.learningObjective: Find net rate after three half-lives small
questions.stem: Gross 100 s^-1, background 12 s^-1; net after three half-lives?
questions.explanation: Net initial is 88, divided by 8 is 11, plus background 12 gives 23. Correct value 23.0; with rounding 23.5 if gross 104. Use 23.0.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_I
questions.topic: Decay constant from a half-life
questions.learningObjective: Explain independence of decay constant from amount
questions.stem: Explain why the decay constant does not depend on how much material is present.

answer.exemplar: The decay constant is a probability per unit time for each nucleus, fixed by the isotope. Adding more nuclei raises N and hence activity, but lambda stays the same.

questions.explanation: Lambda is an intrinsic property of the nuclide. Activity scales with N, but the per-nucleus decay probability does not change with amount.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_I
questions.topic: Time for a sample to fall to a fifth of its starting value
questions.learningObjective: Find time to one fifth with half-life 1 day
questions.stem: Half-life 1.0 day; days to fall to one fifth?
questions.explanation: t = 1 times ln5 over ln2 = 2.322 days. One half-life gives 1 day and one half, not one fifth.

questions.topic: Mean life deduced from a half-life
questions.learningObjective: Find mean life for 100 year half-life
questions.stem: Half-life 100 years; mean life in years?
questions.explanation: Mean life is 100 over 0.693 = 144.3 years. Multiplying by 0.693 gives 69.3, the wrong direction.

questions.topic: Fraction of a technetium-99m dose left after a time
questions.learningObjective: Find fraction after 1 hour
questions.stem: Technetium-99m, 6.0 h half-life; fraction left after 1.0 h?
questions.explanation: Fraction equals 2 to the power minus 1/6, which is 0.891. Linear decay would give 0.917, slightly high.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_I
questions.topic: Time for a strontium-90 activity to fall a thousandfold
questions.learningObjective: Find strontium-90 time to fall a hundredfold
questions.stem: Strontium-90 half-life 28.8 y; years to fall a hundredfold?
questions.explanation: t = 28.8 times log2(100) = 28.8 times 6.644 = 191.4 years. Seven half-lives give 201.6 years and 128-fold.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_I
questions.topic: Finding the impossible row in a decay table
questions.learningObjective: Check a table with 1 s half-life

stimulus.body: Half-life 1 s. Row 1: t=0, N=16. Row 2: t=1 s, N=8. Row 3: t=2 s, N=4. Row 4: t=3 s, N=1. Rows describe one sample.

questions.stem: Which row is inconsistent?
questions.explanation: After three half-lives the count should be 2, not 1. Rows 1 to 3 halve correctly.

questions.topic: Counting uncertainty in a count rate
questions.learningObjective: Compute uncertainty for 25 counts
questions.stem: 25 counts in 5 s; percentage uncertainty in the count rate?
questions.explanation: Uncertainty in counts is 5, divided by 5 s is 1 s^-1, rate is 5 s^-1, so 20 percent. Using 1/sqrt(5) would give 44.7 percent.
